utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88/2-A, the Prosecutor versus Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, can you hear the proceedings in a language you can follow?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Good morning, Mr. President. I can hear the proceedings in the language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Marie-Helene Proulx appearing for the Prosecution, together with Todd Schneider, and our Case Manager, Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we beginning this Status Conference, I would like to address a matter that was brought to our attention recently. On 3 July 2013, Mr. Tolimir filed a motion requesting that his legal advisor, Mr. Aleksandar Gajic -- Mr. Gajic, am I pronouncing our name correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: That was close enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: His legal advisor, Mr. Aleksandar Gajic, be allowed to be present in the courtroom during Status Conferences and be granted a right of audience before the Appeals Chamber at Status Conferences. It is submitted that Mr. Gajic, an assistant professor of law, has served as a legal advisor to Mr. Tolimir during the trial, that he was granted a limited right of audience before the Trial Chamber, and that given Mr. Gajic's responsibilities in this appeal, granting him a right of audience could materially advance the proceedings. The Prosecution responded on 4 July 2013, indicating that it does not object to Mr. Tolimir's request. Pursuant to paragraph 20(A)(ii) of the remuneration scheme for persons assisting indigent, self-represented accused, I am referring to the scheme of 1 April 2010, legal associates have no right of audience before the Court unless the Chamber seized of the case decides otherwise. The Chamber seized of the Tolimir appeal is the Appeals Chamber and Rule 65 bis (B) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence gives me authority to deal with issues arising in the context of Status Conferences, including matters such as courtroom presence and the right of audience during Status Conferences. Considering that Mr. Gajic has served as legal associate to Mr. Tolimir during the trial proceedings and that he's involved in the present appeal, I am satisfied that granting Mr. Gajic a right of audience limited to addressing legal or administrative issues during Status Conferences will be in the interests of justice. However, if you, Mr. Tolimir, wish that Mr. Gajic be granted a right of audience in the appeal proceedings beyond addressing the Pre-appeal Judge at Status Conferences, you should submit a written request to the full Bench of the Appeals Chamber. Mr. Gajic, you may remain in the courtroom today. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the Appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. In the present case, the Notice of Appeal was filed on 11 March 2013. Thus, the Status Conference is taking place before the expiration of the 120-day period specified in Rule 65 bis (B). Today's Status Conference was scheduled by the Scheduling Order issued on 17 June 2013. I would like to begin the Status Conference be inquiring into Mr. Tolimir's health. If you wish, Mr. Tolimir, I can close the session or we can continue in an open session. I see that it's all right with Mr. Tolimir to continue in an open session. Mr. Tolimir, so do tell me anything that you wish to tell me about your state of health. Everything is fine?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Greetings to everybody who is present, and may these proceedings be conducted in accordance with God's will and not mine. Thank you for inquiring. I have consulted with my legal advisor. And thank you for allowing him to be present at this Status Conference and further on. As for my health, my health is constant, as it was during the trial. I do not have any specific concerns or demands in that regard. Now that I have taken the floor, I wish to state the following: Given that the dead-lines were set by the Pre-Appeals Judge, it is stated that following the receipt of the translation of the Judgement, the Appellant, in accordance Rule 108 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, can ask to amend the Notice of Appeal. The translation of the Judgement into the language I understand was filed on the 6th of June, 2013, and the appeal brief was filed on the 28th of June. I hereby make a submission before the Pre-Appeal Judge to set a four-month dead-line for filing any amendments to the appeal brief. In making this request, we took into account the size of the Judgement and the prior practice of this Tribunal in similar cases, cases of similar complexity, such as, for example, the decision of the Pre-Appeal Judge in the Popovic, et al. cases dated 3rd of January, 2012, where the Pre-Appeal Judge decided that a four-month time-period was sufficient for the Appellant to read the translation of the Judgement and give adequate instructions. Mr. President, this is my submission. I have no further issues to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: May I ask the Prosecution's comment on this request.

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have no specific requests in respect to a time-limit. However, it seems to us that the four months requested is excessive. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I will consider your request. I will not issue a ruling on that today, and I will take into account the comment made by the Prosecutor. So in my comments today, we will proceed on the basis of the previous schedule as contemplated, but this is subject to the understanding that I'm aware and I take note of the oral request you have made today. I will consider it and I will, in due course, issue a ruling on that. So let me now turn to the update on the case. On 17 May 2013, I granted, in part, a request by Mr. Tolimir for leave to exceed the word limit and for extension of time for the filing of the appeal brief and ordered that Mr. Tolimir may file an appeal brief totalling not more than 40.000 words no later than 21 June 2013. By the same decision, I also granted an equivalent request from the Prosecution. On 17 June 2013, I granted a further request by Mr. Tolimir for extension of time and allowed Mr. Tolimir to file his appeal brief no later than 28 June 2013. Mr. Tolimir filed his appeal brief on 28 June 2013. Pursuant to my decision of 17 June 2013, the Prosecution's response brief is due on 2 September 2013, and the reply brief, if any, on 20 September, 2013. On 3 July 2013, Mr. Tolimir filed a request to the Appeals Chamber to admit Annexes 1 through 5 to his appeals brief. He submits that the annexes were not originally filed with his appeals brief due to an oversight. The annexes consist of authorities he relies upon in support of his appeal. The Prosecution has not responded to this request, and I would like to ask the Prosecution whether they have any objections to the admission of the annex.

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no concerns with the late filing of the annexes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I take note of the no objection of the Prosecution to this request to admit the annex, and the request is therefore granted. In his appeal brief, Mr. Tolimir indicated his wish to discontinue five of the grounds presented in his Notice of Appeal. Mr. Tolimir also indicated that, due to the word limit, he was unable to present in his appeal brief arguments in support of some of his grounds of appeal. I note that Mr. Tolimir's appeal brief does not include arguments in support of 18 of the grounds presented in his Notice of Appeal. And I would like to ask Mr. Tolimir, or if he prefers Mr. Gajic, to respond, whether I am correct in my understanding that Mr. Tolimir maintenance these grounds of appeal and that he would wish to make further submissions in support of them. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as you know, our announcement of appeal contained 41 grounds for appeal. 40.000 words is too little for each of the grounds to be adequately presented. That is why we limited ourselves to the most essential grounds for appeal. We do not wish to renounce the grounds for appeal. They will remain in the Notice of Appeal, and the appeals brief will be as long as we consider necessary for everything to be duly presented to the Appeals Chamber. Clearly when Mr. Tolimir has perused the Judgement, we may apply for approval for permission from the Appeals Chamber to add possibly additional grounds for appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: My question was whether you maintain your 18 grounds of appeal, and I understand that you do maintain them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. In the circumstances that those grounds of appeal -- Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. The Prosecution would object this. I think the case law is clear that grounds that are not developed in an appeal brief should be deemed to be abandoned. And if Your Honour is minded to grant the request to keep those grounds alive, we would be grateful to have an opportunity to give our submissions in writing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Prosecutor, given the fact that Mr. Tolimir is a self-represented appellant, I think that -- that it would not be quite in the interests of justice not to take those requests into consideration. I would have been much more sympathetic with your approach had Mr. Tolimir been represented by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, our concern is that -- first of all, you granted a substantial increase of the word limit for the appeal brief, which was fully used by the -- by the appellant; and, second of all, our other - main concern, actually - is that we might not have a good opportunity to respond to these grounds of appeal since they are not developed in the appeals brief. So -- yeah, that's our concern -- our concern. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Supposing I grant him some extension and grant you an equivalent number of words to respond to that, I think that would be something which would be fair to both parties. Don't you think so?

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: That would answer our concern. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So let me -- let me sum this up, and I'm glad that we are reaching a common position on that. In the circumstances, and considering that Mr. Tolimir is self-represented, I find that it would be in the interests of justice to allow Mr. Tolimir an extension of time and leave to exceed the word limit to complete his appeal brief and, therefore, he may file a supplement to his appeal brief not exceeding 5.000 words no later than 19 July 2013. And I would grant an equivalent extension to the Prosecution. The Prosecution would therefore -- would file its response brief then no later than 9 September 2013. And thank you for your co-operation, Prosecution. At this point, I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at the time. If I understood correctly Mr. Tolimir's statement, he already indicated that he does not have additional issues. That's correct, isn't it? Thank you. Any additional issues that the Prosecution would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to clarify your -- your ruling. Is your ruling that we would respond in -- we have basically one additional week to file our response but we would not file a separate response to the additional briefing by Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We have no other issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: If that's all right with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PROULX
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. No other issues to raise at this time, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So there are no additional issues that either Mr. Tolimir or the Prosecution would like to raise. And since there are no other matters to be raised, I would just like to thank the parties for their attendance and call these proceedings to a close.
